answer.assistantText: This shows COVID deaths per month for the 10 places with the most deaths overall in the US deaths dataset, using the same top 10 as before. Each row is one place and one month, and if the data starts or ends partway through a month, that month is only partial.
answer.finalSql:
WITH top_places AS (
  SELECT "Province_State"
  FROM "86440223-249d-4b3d-9be4-159a4e615e0a"
  GROUP BY "Province_State"
  ORDER BY SUM("daily_new_deaths") DESC
  LIMIT 10
)
SELECT
  "86440223-249d-4b3d-9be4-159a4e615e0a"."Province_State",
  date_trunc('month', CAST("86440223-249d-4b3d-9be4-159a4e615e0a"."date" AS DATE)) AS "month",
  SUM("86440223-249d-4b3d-9be4-159a4e615e0a"."daily_new_deaths") AS "monthly_deaths"
FROM "86440223-249d-4b3d-9be4-159a4e615e0a"
WHERE "86440223-249d-4b3d-9be4-159a4e615e0a"."Province_State" IN (SELECT "Province_State" FROM top_places)
GROUP BY "86440223-249d-4b3d-9be4-159a4e615e0a"."Province_State", "month"
ORDER BY "86440223-249d-4b3d-9be4-159a4e615e0a"."Province_State", "month"
